# `liber:font@1`

Generated reference for the `liber:font` package (`font.lsidl`). See [the LSIDL language](../../../LSIDL.md).

LiberSystem font package - the installed-face catalogue.  WHAT THIS SERVICE IS FOR, AND WHAT IT DELIBERATELY IS NOT. Deterministic fallback has to enumerate the same set for every client, and a per-process view of "what is installed" is not a set - so the CATALOGUE is service-owned. Parsing, shaping and every glyph and shaping cache are IN-PROCESS, in the calling application, where their allocations are charged to the caller's own Domain and a pathological document harms only the process that asked for it.  SO THIS SERVICE SERVES METADATA AND IDENTITIES, NOT DECODED FACES AND NOT CACHES. What it holds is bounded by the installed-face ceilings, and what it hands over is bytes into a buffer THE CALLER CREATED AND OWNS.

### resource `buffer-object`

A memory object the CALLER created, for the catalogue to fill.  `@kernel(memory-object)` is what makes the `@rights` guard on `resolve-into` refuse a handle of any other kernel object rather than checking rights on whatever it was handed.

An opaque kernel object, transferred as `handle<buffer-object>`.

### record `face-identity`

A face: the content-derived identity of its FILE, and which face within that file.  A COLLECTION IS ONE FILE WITH SEVERAL FACES, so every face in it shares the digest and the index is what tells them apart. The identity is ISSUED BY THE CATALOGUE from the file it read; a client never derives one from a buffer it can write, because a client that rewrote its own buffer would otherwise have changed what an identity names.

| field | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `digest` | `list<u8>` |  |
| `index` | `u32` |  |

### record `face-record`

What the catalogue publishes about a face: its identity and its DECLARED metadata.  DECLARED AND NOT DERIVED. Getting family, style, axes, face index and format out of OpenType bytes is PARSING, and a parser inside the catalogue would be a second, unprofiled, hostile-input parser written before the item that authorises one. The record is a checked-in declaration staged beside the face, validated and digested by the staging tool; whether it is TRUE is checked by the profiled parser, which is the only component allowed to read a font.  ITS ENCODED SIZE IS BOUNDED at 256 bytes, which is what makes a full `list` reply arithmetic rather than hope: 64 faces at 256 bytes plus a reserved 4096-byte envelope for the list count, the result tag, the correlation id and whatever framing a reply grows later.

### record `face-bytes`

What `resolve-info` answers: how big the face is, and which publication that answer is about.  IT ALLOCATES NOTHING, which is the whole reason resolve is two operations: in this kernel a memory object is charged to the Domain that CREATED it and stays charged after the handle moves, so a catalogue that created the buffer would grow without bound under a client that kept asking. The caller must be told the size before it can create the object.

| field | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `identity` | `face-identity` |  |
| `generation` | `u64` |  |
| `length` | `u64` |  |

### variant `resolve-outcome`

What `resolve-into` did.  THE REFUSALS ARE TYPED AND CARRY WHAT THE CALLER NEEDS TO RETRY, because "invalid" would leave a caller unable to tell a stale generation from a buffer one byte too small.

| tag | case | payload | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `filled` | `u64` | The bytes are in the caller's object; the value is how many were written. |
| 1 | `stale` | `u64` | The publication moved, or the bytes under the published identity are not the bytes that identity names. The value is the generation that is current now: re-ask.  THE SECOND CASE IS NOT THE GENERATION'S. The generation moves only once the catalogue has PROCESSED a watch hint, and a hint can be dropped - so an admitted read under a still-current old generation could return a REPLACEMENT's bytes under the previous identity. `resolve-into` digests what it actually read and compares it with the published identity; different is this same refusal, and the catalogue rescans immediately rather than waiting for a hint that may never arrive. |
| 2 | `too-small` | `u64` | The object is smaller than the face. The value is the length required. |

## Interfaces

### interface `font-catalogue`

What an application holds: enumerate the installed faces, and get a face's bytes into a buffer of its own.  IT NEVER HOLDS StorageService AUTHORITY and never scans a directory. A client without this capability reaches no face at all.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `list` | `list() -> result<list<face-record>, error>` | Every installed face, as bounded metadata records. One message: the reply bound is arithmetic from the two ceilings above it. |
| 2 | `resolve-info` | `resolve-info(identity: face-identity) -> result<face-bytes, error>` | How long a face is, and which publication that answer is about. Allocates nothing. |
| 3 | `resolve-into` | `resolve-into(identity: face-identity, generation: u64, target: handle<buffer-object>) -> result<resolve-outcome, error>` | Fill a memory object the CALLER created with the face's bytes.  THE HANDLE IS ATTENUATED AT THE CALLER, before the send: `SYS_HANDLE_DUPLICATE` narrows and never widens, so the caller creates the object, duplicates a handle down to map, write and transfer, and passes the COPY - keeping the original, so the send consuming the copy costs it nothing. Without `duplicate` the catalogue cannot make a second handle and keep it after closing the one it was given, which is the property the retained-face gates rest on.  `transfer` IS present and cannot be otherwise: the typed transport consumes request handles that way. That the catalogue must not pass the object on is a code obligation with a gate, not a right it lacks - said plainly, because a plan that claims a rights bit it cannot obtain has a security argument that is decoration.  The generation is the one `resolve-info` answered about, and it is what closes the race between the two calls. |
| 4 | `subscribe` | `subscribe() -> stream<generation-event>` | Learn that the published set changed, without polling. |

### interface `font-catalogue-admin`

The operator's interface: recovery after a dropped watch hint.  A SECOND SERVE ROOT ON THE CATALOGUE ITSELF, tagged `ADMIN`, minted at its start beside the client one - the shape StorageService's `ADMIN` root already has. `rescan` is NOT on the client interface: authority to READ a font must not become authority to make the machine work, and the live-endpoint ceiling bounds endpoints rather than requests on one.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `rescan` | `rescan() -> result<rescan-outcome, error>` | Re-read the directory now. At most one in flight; every completed scan re-arms a delay, whatever it found. |
